outcomes: A GitHub Actions workflow adds one step, uses: Putnami/observe-action@v1, after its tests and reads the change summary in its log, with no install line to copy
With a Putnami token, the same step uploads the change evidence document and posts the commit status and the summary note on the pull request
A release of the action moves the v1 tag, so a workflow that names v1 runs the newest compatible action
nonGoals: Windows runners: the action fails with a message that names Linux and macOS
Checking out the repository or changing its fetch depth: putnami observe deepens a shallow clone itself
Uploading the evidence document as a workflow artifact: the step gives its path as an output for actions/upload-artifact
GitLab CI, which has no Marketplace action

requirements.text: The action runs one bash step on a Linux or macOS runner. It installs the Putnami CLI with https://putnami.dev/install.sh, puts ~/.putnami/bin on the PATH, and installs @putnami/observe in the user scope, all from the channel input, stable when empty, which reads latest as putnami upgrade reads it; it installs @putnami/cloud too when the token input is set. On a Windows runner the step fails with a message that names Linux and macOS, and installs nothing.

A channel input that is a version, or outside the channel alphabet of putnami init (a lowercase letter or a digit, then lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', 64 characters at most), fails the step before any install: the release lines do not share one version.

The step runs putnami observe with --evidence at a file under RUNNER_TEMP and gives that path as the evidence output. Each of the junit, coverage, sbom, base-sbom and base inputs that is not empty becomes the flag of the same name with its value; an empty input passes no flag. The action checks out nothing and sets no fetch depth.

With the token input set, the step runs putnami observe with --upload and PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN set to the token, and the publish input defaults to true; without it, publish defaults to false. publish set to true or false overrides the default. publish true adds --publish, and the run's GITHUB_TOKEN reaches putnami observe only with the token too: only then does the job need statuses: write and pull-requests: write. Another publish value fails the step before the install.

The token input and the run's token reach putnami observe only, never the installer or the extension installs. A PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN the job sets in the step's environment is not read, and a PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN there without the token input gives a warning that names the token input.

A release of version X.Y.Z, a semantic version without a pre-release or build suffix, replaces the root of the Putnami/observe-action default branch with the action directory and the repository licence, commits it, tags it vX.Y.Z and moves vX to it in one atomic push: the branch and both tags move together or none does. A version that is not X.Y.Z stops the release before any tag is read, and a vX.Y.Z tag that already exists stops it before any push.

The release workflow runs on a manual dispatch from main only, in the GitHub environment observe-action, which holds the only token that writes to Putnami/observe-action; the environment's branch policy allows main only, so a dispatch from another branch gets no token.
